issues.body: The script builds and streams each leg's human-readable output independently, but it never captures or compares the released and upstream triple counts and digests. Each binary only checks repeated parses against its own warm-up. Consequently, two parsers that deterministically produce different triple streams both succeed and the one-command A/B exits 0, despite README.md and the research record presenting equal count plus digest as the load-bearing differential invariant. This is materially the same first major finding from round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Have every compared leg emit a machine-readable result (the existing --json support can be used), compare both triples and digest against the released reference in ab.sh, and exit nonzero while reporting both sides on mismatch. Add a small script-level test or mutation check that deliberately changes one digest and proves the A/B command fails.
issues.title: The A/B command still does not enforce output equivalence

verdict.summary: Round 4 fixes the attribution-provenance defect: the global 9af7d59 substitution now updates the generated package description as well as dependency revisions. The load-bearing differential remains observational, however. ab.sh runs each parser independently and never compares the released and upstream triple counts or digests, so a stable wrong-answer regression still exits successfully. One of two prior major findings remains, so progress is improving but the PR is not yet approvable.
